-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

   Method: Linear-phase, robust, non-linear smoothing (LRNS)

Reference: Hattingh, M., L. Loubser, D. Nagtegaal - "Computer K-index
           estimation by a new linear-phase, robust, non-linear smoothing
           method", Geophys. J. Int. (1989) 99, 533-547.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Note:  The version of the LRNS K-index algorithm on this diskette is the 
       "public domain" release.  There is a commercially available 
       "industrialized" version in existence.
       The two versions are said to produce comparable results.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

                                Files on diskette:

     K_FILTER.FOR - Fortran source code of routine to estimate solar-regular 
                    (SR) variation of X and Y components of the geomagnetic  
                    field.

             Notes: Useage of the routine is described within the source code.

                    When the quiet day pattern occurs in the middle of a UT
                    day the "q index" should be set to "M".  This will be
                    appropriate for observatories near the 0 degree longitude
                    such as in Europe and Africa.  At such an observatory 
                    "q start" is the minute of the day when the field begins 
                    its regular variation pattern and "q end" is the minute 
                    when the variations finish.
                    For example qindex=M, qstart=300, qend=1009

                    When the quiet day pattern occurs at the end of a UT day
                    the "q index" should be set to "E".  This will be for
                    observatories near the 180 degree longitude such as in
                    the Pacific, eastern Asia and Australia.  At these
                    observatories "q start" is the minute of the day when
                    night-time conditions begin and "q end" is when the field
                    begins its regular variation.
                    For example qindex=E, qstart=360, qend=1080

                    Type "E" data are the most difficult to match.  If the UT
                    hours are shifted to to make it a type "M" curve better
                    results can be obtained.  Withe type "E" curves the 
                    "qstart" and "qend" values are more critical as well as
                    trying to match the first few and last few values of a UT
                    day during quiet days.

                    K_FILTER calls the double precision random number  
                    generator function, random().  The random numbers actually
                    required by K_FILTER are between -1 and +1 and can be
                    either real or double precision. 
                    The purpose of this is to stimulate the adaption in the
                    case of very quiet days.
                    A random number generator which may be adapted for use in
                    k_filter (with output in [0,1]) is included in the file
                    spectral.for in the AGSO directory of the diskette.  

                    The resultant SR produced by K_FILTER can be subtracted 
                    from the original data and the difference scaled directly 
                    using user supplied routines.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                End of file
